title: Orthogonal decomposition of smooth Dolbeault forms
statement: All vector spaces below are over the complex field $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $M$ be a compact complex manifold without boundary of complex dimension $n\geq0$, with a smooth positive definite Hermitian metric on its complex tangent bundle. For integers $p,q$, write $A^{p,q}(M)$ for the complex vector space of smooth complex differential forms of type $(p,q)$, with this space zero unless $0\leq p,q\leq n$. The type decomposition of the exterior derivative is $d=\partial+\bar\partial$, where $\bar\partial:A^{p,q}\to A^{p,q+1}$ and $\bar\partial^2=0$. Equip smooth forms with the $L^2$ inner product obtained by integrating the pointwise metric against its volume form. Let $\bar\partial^*:A^{p,q+1}\to A^{p,q}$ be its formal adjoint, characterized by $\langle\bar\partial u,v\rangle_{L^2}=\langle u,\bar\partial^*v\rangle_{L^2}$ for smooth forms of these types. Put $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$. There is an orthogonal direct sum of spaces of smooth forms $$A^{p,q}(M)=\ker(\Delta_{\bar\partial}|_{A^{p,q}(M)})\ \mathbin{\oplus^{\perp}}\ \bar\partial A^{p,q-1}(M)\ \mathbin{\oplus^{\perp}}\ \bar\partial^* A^{p,q+1}(M).$$ The summands are actual images on smooth forms, without taking closures.

source.place: WANTED locally: Wenrui Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §6.2, Theorem 6.7, printed pp.23--24; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. The Dolbeault orthogonal decomposition, not its subsequent cohomology corollary.

proof.text: If $p$ or $q$ is outside $[0,n]$, all three subspaces in the asserted equality lie in the zero space $A^{p,q}$ and the equality follows. If $M$ is empty it is equally immediate. When $n=0$, a compact zero-dimensional manifold is a finite discrete set; only $A^{0,0}$ can be nonzero, all differentials vanish, and the harmonic space is all of $A^{0,0}$. Hence assume $n\geq1$ and $0\leq p,q\leq n$. Write $D=\bar\partial$ and $P=DD^*+D^*D$ on this type.

source.place: Theorem 6.7, printed pp.23--24; edge cases written out by Q53.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-dolbeault-laplacian-elliptic], $D^*$ preserves smoothness and $P$ is an elliptic differential operator on $E^{p,q}$, also after realification. Adjointness gives $\langle Pa,b\rangle=\langle D^*a,D^*b\rangle+\langle Da,Db\rangle=\langle a,Pb\rangle$. Regard $E^{p,q}$ as a real bundle with fibre metric $\operatorname{Re}\langle-,-\rangle$ and $M$ as its oriented real manifold of dimension $2n$; holomorphic charts preserve its complex orientation. The real $L^2$ pairing is the real part of the Hermitian pairing. Thus $P$ is its own formal real adjoint. Apply [lem-sfb-elliptic-smooth-fredholm-decomposition] with $E=F$ this real bundle and $k=2$. For every smooth $a\in A^{p,q}$ it gives smooth $h,w\in A^{p,q}$ with $Ph=0$ and $a=h+Pw=h+D(D^*w)+D^*(Dw)$. The two displayed primitives have types $(p,q-1)$ and $(p,q+1)$; at the boundary a primitive in a zero type is zero.

source.place: Lemmas 6.2, 6.4 and Theorem 6.5(4), printed pp.21,23, applied to the type bundle; assembly for Theorem 6.7.

proof.text: For $Ph=0$, adjointness gives $0=\langle Ph,h\rangle=\|D^*h\|_{L^2}^2+\|Dh\|_{L^2}^2$. Nonnegativity implies $D^*h=Dh=0$. Indeed a nonzero smooth form has strictly positive pointwise squared norm on some coordinate neighbourhood, whose smooth positive metric volume makes its integral positive. Thus zero $L^2$ norm forces the form itself to be zero. Consequently $\langle Du,h\rangle=\langle u,D^*h\rangle=0$ and $\langle h,D^*v\rangle=\langle Dh,v\rangle=0$ for arbitrary smooth primitives $u,v$. Harmonic forms are orthogonal to both images for the complex Hermitian pairing.

source.place: §6.1 after Lemma 6.2, kernel identity; Theorem 6.7, orthogonality argument written out.

proof.text: For arbitrary $u\in A^{p,q-1}$ and $v\in A^{p,q+1}$, $\langle Du,D^*v\rangle=\langle D(Du),v\rangle=0$ by $D^2=0$. Hence the two smooth images are orthogonal. Step 2 shows that the three subspaces span $A^{p,q}$ with actual smooth primitives $u=D^*w$ and $v=Dw$. To prove directness, if $h+x+y=0$ with $h$ harmonic, $x\in\operatorname{im}D$ and $y\in\operatorname{im}D^*$, pair this equation separately with $h,x,y$. Pairwise orthogonality gives $\|h\|^2=\|x\|^2=\|y\|^2=0$, so all vanish by step 3. Subtracting two decompositions gives uniqueness of their three summand components. This proves the asserted complex orthogonal direct sum without any closure.

source.place: Theorem 6.7, printed pp.23--24; exact/coexact orthogonality and directness written out by Q53.

proof_origin.place: Kong Theorem 6.7 via Lemmas 6.2,6.4 and Theorem 6.5(4), read online; local source WANTED. Q53 writes out the assembly and realification.
